findings.evidence: Physlib has the general bilinear form already: `upstream/Physlib/Physlib/Relativity/Tensors/RealTensor/Vector/MinkowskiProduct.lean:156` `minkowskiProduct_eq_timeComponent_spatialPart (p q) : ⟪p, q⟫ₘ = p.timeComponent * q.timeComponent - ⟪p.spatialPart, q.spatialPart⟫_ℝ`. The PR's own consumer wants the spatial part as a whole vector: at `MinkowskiProductExtensions.lean:151-154` `hps : p.spatialPart = P • e₀` and `hp's : p'.spatialPart = P' • u` now need `spatialPart_ofTimeAndTwoSpatial_eq` plus `module`, whereas the comment this PR removes (diff lines `-- `Physlib` has no constructor from a time component and a spatial part ... hold by `rfl``) records that these held definitionally for a vector built directly from its components.
findings.fix: Define `ofTimeAndSpatial {d} (x : ℝ) (s : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : Lorentz.Vector d` with `timeComponent_ofTimeAndSpatial = x` and `spatialPart_ofTimeAndSpatial = s`, prove `⟪ofTimeAndSpatial x s, ofTimeAndSpatial x' s'⟫ₘ = x * x' - ⟪s, s'⟫_ℝ` in one step from Physlib's `minkowskiProduct_eq_timeComponent_spatialPart`, and obtain the three-coefficient frame as `ofTimeAndSpatial x (y • EuclideanSpace.basisFun _ ℝ i + z • EuclideanSpace.basisFun _ ℝ j)` (keeping the `i ≠ j` diagonal form as a corollary only if a caller needs it). Sub/add lemmas then follow from linearity.
findings.issue: `ofTimeAndTwoSpatial i j x y z` is a special case of a constructor from a time component and an arbitrary spatial vector. Consequently `minkowskiProduct_ofTimeAndTwoSpatial_eq` only covers two vectors built from the same pair `i ≠ j` (it cannot state `⟪ofTimeAndTwoSpatial i j .., ofTimeAndTwoSpatial k l ..⟫ₘ`), takes six scalars plus `hij`, and needs a long basis `simp only`; `ofTimeAndTwoSpatial_sub_ofTimeAndTwoSpatial_eq` is a bespoke restatement of linearity.

summary: The GPD kinematics statements sit at the right level, but the new Minkowski-vector constructor is under-general: `ofTimeAndTwoSpatial` fixes a time component and exactly two indexed spatial coefficients where a `(timeComponent, spatialPart)` constructor is the natural form, directly supported by Physlib's existing product lemma and wanted by the PR's own consumer.
